intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM - collect luggage, pick up any pre-booked rental car or take TheBus (Oahu's public transit, ~$3/ride) to your accommodation. Check in or store luggage if room isn't ready.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach (free entry) - just a short bus or walk from most Honolulu accommodations. Relax on the sand, swim in the calm waters, and let the kids splash around. Rent a bodyboard from a local vendor (~$10/hour) for extra fun.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue, Waikiki's main strip. Watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, nightly shows around sunset). Grab dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing - look for local plate lunch counters inside the terminal (~$8-10)
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In near Waikiki - iconic local plate lunch spot, combo plates from $10-13, great for families
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon in Waikiki - fresh udon noodles from ~$8, toppings extra, very family-friendly and budget-conscious

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 11:20 AM arrival. Pick up a reusable TheBus pass ($70/month unlimited or $3/ride) to save on transport. Stop at a local ABC Store or Don Quijote supermarket to stock up on snacks and drinks for the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (entry $5/person, free for kids under 3). Hike the iconic 1.6-mile round-trip trail to the summit crater for panoramic views of Honolulu and the coastline. Start early (opens at 6 AM) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off at Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) - a quieter, family-friendly alternative to Waikiki with calm, shallow waters and free parking nearby. Snorkel gear can be rented locally (~$10-15/set).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Chinatown Honolulu for affordable eats and local culture. Browse the open-air markets and pick up fresh tropical fruits. Enjoy a budget dinner at one of the many local eateries.

meals.breakfast: Bogart's Cafe near Diamond Head - acai bowls and breakfast plates from $9-13, great fuel before the hike
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the supermarket to enjoy at Kaimana Beach - saves $15-20 per person
meals.dinner: Little Village Noodle House in Chinatown - generous portions of Chinese-Hawaiian fusion from $12-16 per dish, great for sharing

day_by_day.notes: August weather averages around 16.8°C (62°F) in the early morning - bring a light layer for the Diamond Head hike. The trail has some steep sections with stairs; manageable for most kids over 5. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus or drive to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve (entry $25/adult, free for Hawaii residents and children under 13). One of Oahu's best snorkeling spots with abundant sea turtles and tropical fish. Arrive early - the bay reaches capacity quickly and reservations are recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or bus along the scenic Windward Coast to Lanikai Beach - consistently rated one of the world's most beautiful beaches. The calm, turquoise water is perfect for families. Walk the Lanikai Pillbox Trail (~1.8 miles round trip) for stunning aerial views.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Kailua Town for dinner and a browse of local shops. Kailua is a charming, laid-back beach town with great affordable dining options.

meals.breakfast: Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua - famous for red velvet pancakes and local breakfast dishes, ~$12-16/person
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua - grab deli sandwiches, wraps, and fresh juices to enjoy at Lanikai Beach (~$10-14)
meals.dinner: Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen in Kailua - legendary macadamia nut pancakes and local plates, dinner from ~$14-18

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations (book at least 2 days ahead at hanaumabaystatepark.com). Snorkel gear is available to rent on-site (~$12). The bay is closed on Tuesdays. August can bring occasional rain showers on the windward side - pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center on Oahu's North Shore (admission ~$60-80/adult, $50-60/child - look for online discount codes to bring costs down). Explore six authentic Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Highly educational and interactive for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the North Shore and visit Sunset Beach and Waimea Bay (both free). In August, the summer swells are calm and perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Waimea Bay's famous rock jump is a thrill for older kids and adults.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the famous Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku for a North Shore institution experience before heading back to Honolulu.

meals.breakfast: Grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery on the way out of Honolulu - a must-try Hawaii treat, ~$1.50 each
meals.lunch: Included with Polynesian Cultural Center admission (buffet lunch package) or pack your own to save money
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku - famous garlic shrimp plates ~$15, cash only, iconic North Shore experience

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is a splurge but offers exceptional family value and educational content. Look for Groupon or AAA discounts. The drive around the island is about 1.5-2 hours each way - consider renting a car for this day if using public transit otherwise. Pack sunscreen and reef-safe products.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or take a ferry to Maui (inter-island flights on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest from ~$60-100 one way if booked in advance). Alternatively, dedicate this day to exploring more of Oahu. If flying to Maui, arrive and check into budget accommodation (Hostel Maui or vacation rental ~$80-120/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Baldwin Beach Park in Paia, Maui - a beautiful, less-crowded beach popular with locals. The town of Paia itself is a charming hippie surf town with great affordable food and unique shops.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Paia Town, browse local boutiques, and enjoy a relaxed evening meal. Watch the sunset from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Airport breakfast or pack snacks for the flight - grab a smoothie at Honolulu airport (~$8-10)
meals.lunch: Flatbread Company in Paia - wood-fired pizzas with local ingredients, ~$16-22 per pizza to share
meals.dinner: Milagros Food Company in Paia - Mexican-Hawaiian fusion with outdoor seating, tacos and burritos from ~$14-18

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights well in advance for the best budget prices. If budget is very tight, consider spending all 10 days on Oahu and skipping inter-island travel. Maui accommodation options: Banana Bungalow Maui Hostel (~$35-50/dorm) or budget vacation rentals via Airbnb.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Road to Hana (Hana Highway) - one of Hawaii's most iconic scenic drives. Stop at Twin Falls (free, easy 20-minute hike), Waikamoi Nature Trail, and Garden of Eden Arboretum (~$20/car). The lush rainforest scenery is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Road to Hana, stopping at Wai'anapanapa State Park (reservation required, $5/person parking) - famous for its dramatic black sand beach, sea caves, and blowholes. Swim in the refreshing freshwater cave pools.
day_by_day.evening: Reach Hana Town for a relaxed evening. Visit Hasegawa General Store, a Hana institution. Watch the sunset from Hamoa Beach, one of Maui's most beautiful.

meals.breakfast: Charley's Restaurant in Paia before departing - hearty breakfast plates from $12-16
meals.lunch: Roadside food stands along the Hana Highway - fresh coconut, banana bread from Aunty Sandy's (~$5-8), and local snacks
meals.dinner: Hana Ranch Restaurant - casual dining with local ingredients, plates from $18-25, or pack a picnic dinner to enjoy at Hamoa Beach

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is about 65 miles but takes 3-4 hours one way due to 600+ curves and 59 bridges. Start early (by 7-8 AM) to avoid traffic and have maximum time at stops. Reserve Wai'anapanapa State Park in advance at hawaiistateparks.reserveamerica.com. Bring motion sickness medication if needed for kids.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (3:30 AM) for the sunrise at Haleakala National Park summit (10,023 feet). Entry fee is $35/car (valid for 3 days). The sunrise above the clouds is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Reservations for sunrise viewing are required - book at recreation.gov well in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending from Haleakala, stop at Kula for lunch and explore the upcountry farms and lavender fields. Visit Ali'i Kula Lavender Farm (free to walk, small fee for tours) for stunning views and unique photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kihei or Wailea on Maui's sunny south shore. Enjoy the calmer, sunnier weather and beautiful beaches. Kamaole Beach Parks I, II, and III are all free and family-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Pack hot coffee in a thermos and granola bars for the summit - it's cold at the top (can be near freezing), so warm food is essential
meals.lunch: Kula Lodge Restaurant - scenic upcountry dining with views, sandwiches and plates from $14-18
meals.dinner: Coconut's Fish Cafe in Kihei - award-winning fish tacos and plates from $12-16, very popular with locals and visitors

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise reservations open 60 days in advance and sell out fast - this is critical to book early. Bring warm layers for the summit (temperatures can be 40-50°F/4-10°C even in August). The descent takes about 1.5 hours. After the early morning, plan for a relaxed afternoon as the family will be tired.

day_by_day.morning: Fly to the Big Island of Hawaii (inter-island flight ~$60-100). Check into budget accommodation in Hilo or Volcano Village (vacation rental or hostel ~$80-120/night). Hilo is the rainier, lush side of the island with a charming old-town feel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hilo's highlights: Rainbow Falls (free), Boiling Pots (free), and the beautiful Liliuokalani Gardens (free Japanese garden). Visit the Hilo Farmers Market (open daily, best on Wednesdays and Saturdays) for fresh tropical fruits, local crafts, and affordable snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through downtown Hilo, browse the historic buildings, and enjoy a relaxed dinner. Hilo has some of the most affordable dining on any Hawaiian island.

meals.breakfast: Airport snack or pack from accommodation
meals.lunch: Hilo Farmers Market - fresh fruit, local snacks, and prepared foods from $3-10, excellent budget option
meals.dinner: Cafe Pesto in Hilo - wood-fired pizzas and pasta with local ingredients, ~$16-22 per pizza to share, great family atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Hilo receives significant rainfall (176+ mm in August) so pack rain gear. The lush, green landscape is a result of this rainfall and is absolutely stunning. The Big Island is the largest Hawaiian island and requires a car to explore properly - rent one at the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (entry $35/car, valid 7 days). Start with the Kilauea Visitor Center to understand the volcanic landscape. Walk the Kilauea Iki Trail (4-mile loop, 2-3 hours) through a hardened lava lake - an otherworldly experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive Chain of Craters Road (19 miles one way, free with park entry) to see ancient lava flows meeting the ocean. Stop at Holei Sea Arch, lava tube formations, and petroglyphs. Visit Thurston Lava Tube (Nahuku) - a 500-year-old lava tube you can walk through.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Kilauea Overlook at dusk to see the volcanic glow from Halemaumau Crater - particularly dramatic after dark. This is one of Hawaii's most memorable experiences.

meals.breakfast: Volcano House Restaurant inside the park - breakfast buffet ~$20/adult, or pack your own breakfast to save money
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at one of the park's scenic overlooks - buy supplies the night before in Hilo
meals.dinner: Thai Thai Restaurant in Volcano Village just outside the park - authentic Thai food, generous portions from $13-17, very popular with park visitors

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park is the highlight experience available in your trip details. Check nps.gov/havo for current volcanic activity updates before visiting. The park is open 24 hours. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for lava field walking. Volcanic smog (vog) can affect air quality - those with respiratory issues should check conditions. Kids will be amazed by the alien landscape.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Punaluu Black Sand Beach (free) - one of Hawaii's most unique beaches with jet-black volcanic sand. Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu) frequently rest on the beach - maintain the required 10-foot distance. A magical, memorable experience for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kona side for your final afternoon. Stop at Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area (free, $10 parking) - consistently rated one of Hawaii's best beaches with calm, clear water perfect for swimming and snorkeling. A beautiful farewell to Hawaii.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kona before heading to the airport for your return flight. Browse Ali'i Drive in Kona for last-minute souvenirs at affordable prices. ABC Stores offer budget-friendly Hawaii souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Ken's House of Pancakes in Hilo - a 24-hour local institution, massive portions from $10-14, perfect hearty final morning meal
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and fruit from the farmers market for the drive to Kona
meals.dinner: Da Poke Shack in Kona - fresh, local poke bowls from $12-16, one of the best poke spots in Hawaii for a memorable final meal

day_by_day.notes: Check flight times and plan the day accordingly. Return rental car with a full tank (gas stations near airports are more expensive). Pack any fresh fruit or local food items that are allowed through TSA. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaii adventure! Total estimated budget per adult (excluding flights): $150-200/day covering accommodation, food, activities, and transport.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM — no morning activities scheduled. After landing, collect baggage and arrange ground transportation to your accommodation area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park and freshen up. Take a relaxed stroll around the Buena Park area to get oriented. Visit a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first evening — explore Downtown Disney or the Anaheim GardenWalk for a casual family-friendly atmosphere, window shopping, and light entertainment to wind down after travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bite at the airport before or after landing — try a local café or sandwich counter inside the terminal.
meals.lunch: Pick up a casual meal near the hotel — Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers or In-N-Out Burger on Beach Blvd for a quick, affordable, family-friendly option.
meals.dinner: BJ's Restaurant & Brewhouse at Anaheim GardenWalk — mid-range pricing, large menu with something for everyone, relaxed atmosphere perfect after a travel day.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:20 AM, keep Day 1 light and low-key. Prioritize rest and recovery so the family is energized for the full Hawaii experience starting Day 2. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance as standard check-in is typically 3:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Knott's Berry Farm when it opens at 10:00 AM — located just minutes from the hotel on Beach Blvd. Enjoy family-friendly rides, the Ghost Town area, and classic Knott's attractions. Great for all ages and a perfect warm-up activity day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Knott's Berry Farm through the afternoon. Hit the bigger thrill rides like GhostRider and Hangtime, or let younger kids enjoy Camp Snoopy. Take a mid-afternoon break with a famous Knott's boysenberry treat.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel to rest and freshen up, then enjoy a relaxed dinner nearby before an early bedtime to prepare for upcoming packed days.

meals.breakfast: Hotel continental breakfast or grab pastries and coffee at a nearby Starbucks on Orangethorpe Ave before heading to the park.
meals.lunch: Mrs. Knott's Chicken Dinner Restaurant inside the park — a Knott's institution famous for its fried chicken, biscuits, and boysenberry pie. Mid-range and worth every penny.
meals.dinner: Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que on Beach Blvd — hearty BBQ portions, family-friendly, and reasonably priced for a sit-down meal.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Knott's Berry Farm tickets online in advance to save money and skip ticket lines. Check the park's calendar for any special August events or shows. Wear comfortable shoes and bring sunscreen — August in Southern California can be warm and sunny.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Huntington Beach (Surf City USA) — about 20 minutes from the hotel. Arrive early to claim a good spot on the wide sandy beach. Let the kids play in the waves and build sandcastles while adults relax. Rent boogie boards from a local surf shop on Main Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Huntington Beach Pier and explore the lively Main Street strip with its surf shops, boutiques, and casual eateries. If the family is up for it, book a beginner surf lesson through Corky Carroll's Surf School — a fun and memorable experience for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the pier — one of the most beautiful views in Southern California. Then head to Main Street for dinner before driving back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Pick up breakfast burritos from a local taqueria near the hotel or grab items from a grocery store for a quick beach-ready meal.
meals.lunch: Sugar Shack Café on Main Street, Huntington Beach — a beloved local breakfast and lunch spot with hearty portions and a beachy vibe. Expect a short wait but well worth it.
meals.dinner: Wahoo's Fish Taco on Main Street — casual, affordable, and perfectly on-theme with fresh fish tacos, burritos, and bowls. Great for families.

day_by_day.notes: Huntington Beach is a great preview of the beach lifestyle you'll experience in Hawaii. Parking is available in city lots near the pier — arrive before 10 AM to avoid peak crowds and higher parking fees. Bring towels, sunscreen SPF 50+, and water shoes for the kids.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach — about 25 minutes from the hotel. This world-class aquarium is perfect for families with exhibits on tropical Pacific, Northern Pacific, and Southern California/Baja habitats. A wonderful educational preview of the marine life you'll snorkel with in Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the aquarium, explore the Long Beach waterfront. Walk along the Rainbow Harbor, visit the historic Queen Mary ship (exterior viewing is free), or let the kids play at the nearby Shoreline Village. Take a short harbor cruise if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Buena Park and spend the evening at Medieval Times Dinner & Tournament — a unique, family-friendly dinner show experience located just minutes from the hotel on Beach Blvd.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the hotel or stop at a local diner on the way to Long Beach.
meals.lunch: Parker's Lighthouse Restaurant at Shoreline Village, Long Beach — waterfront dining with fresh seafood, burgers, and salads. Mid-range pricing with great harbor views.
meals.dinner: Medieval Times Dinner & Tournament — the dinner is included with the show ticket. Expect roasted chicken, soup, and sides served without utensils for a fun, immersive experience. Book tickets online in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Aquarium of the Pacific offers family combo tickets that provide good value. Arrive when it opens at 9:00 AM to beat school groups and tour buses. Medieval Times tickets should be booked at least a few days in advance, especially for August when demand is high.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Getty Center in Los Angeles — a stunning hilltop museum with world-class art collections and panoramic views of LA. Free admission (parking fee applies). Great for older kids and adults; younger children will enjoy the outdoor gardens and architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Santa Monica Pier and the Third Street Promenade. Enjoy the iconic pier with its Pacific Park amusement rides, street performers, and ocean views. Let the kids ride the solar-powered Ferris wheel and play arcade games.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Santa Monica Beach at golden hour, then head to the Third Street Promenade for dinner and some light shopping before the drive back to Buena Park.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and pastries at a local café near the hotel before heading out for the drive to LA.
meals.lunch: Eggslut at the Original Farmers Market on Fairfax (on the way to Santa Monica) — famous for creative egg sandwiches and comfort food. Casual and mid-range.
meals.dinner: The Lobster at Santa Monica Pier — a splurge-worthy dinner with fresh seafood and stunning ocean views. Slightly above mid-range but perfect for a special family evening. Alternatively, Blue Plate Taco on Ocean Ave for a more budget-friendly option.

day_by_day.notes: Traffic in LA can be significant — leave the hotel by 8:30 AM to reach the Getty Center when it opens at 10:00 AM. Use Google Maps or Waze for real-time traffic updates. Parking at the Getty is $20. Consider using the Metro Expo Line from downtown LA to Santa Monica to avoid parking hassles at the pier.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Universal Studios Hollywood — about 35 minutes from the hotel. Arrive at opening time (typically 9:00 AM) to experience the most popular attractions before crowds build. Must-dos include The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, Jurassic World ride, and the Studio Tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Universal Studios. Catch a live show or stunt performance, and let the kids enjoy the lower-level attractions. Take a break mid-afternoon with a snack and some shade.
day_by_day.evening: Wrap up at Universal CityWalk for dinner and entertainment before heading back to the hotel. CityWalk has a great mix of restaurants, shops, and live music.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before heading out — pack some granola bars or fruit for the car ride.
meals.lunch: Three Broomsticks inside The Wizarding World of Harry Potter — themed food including Great Feast platters, Butterbeer, and pumpkin juice. A fun, immersive lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. at Universal CityWalk — family-friendly, themed restaurant with shrimp dishes, burgers, and a fun atmosphere. Mid-range pricing.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Universal Studios tickets online well in advance for the best pricing. Consider the Express Pass if budget allows — it significantly reduces wait times. August is peak season so the park will be busy; arriving at opening time is essential. Wear comfortable shoes and bring a light jacket for air-conditioned indoor attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — this is a full-day featured experience. Note: Hanauma Bay is located on Oahu, Hawaii. If this is a day trip by flight, depart early from LAX. Alternatively, if the itinerary includes a flight to Hawaii on this day, arrive and head directly to Hanauma Bay in the afternoon. Explore the pristine marine sanctuary with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling and beach time at Hanauma Bay. Watch the mandatory educational video about reef conservation before entering the water. Rent snorkel gear on-site if needed. The bay is sheltered and calm — ideal for families with children.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Hawaii accommodation and settle in. Take a gentle evening walk along a nearby beach to soak in the island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or airport before departure to Hawaii.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for Hanauma Bay — outside food is allowed. Alternatively, grab plate lunches from a nearby food truck or local deli on the way to the bay.
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood in Honolulu — a beloved local spot famous for fresh poke bowls. Casual, affordable, and authentically Hawaiian. Perfect first dinner on the island.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations — book online at least 2 days in advance as daily visitor numbers are strictly limited. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Entry fee is $25 per adult; children under 12 are free. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned to protect the coral. Arrive early as parking fills up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures. Located on the North Shore of Oahu, the center opens at 11:45 AM. Explore the Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Aotearoa (Maori) villages. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire making, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center villages. Watch live cultural demonstrations and performances throughout the afternoon. Don't miss the canoe pageant on the lagoon — a spectacular floating parade of Polynesian cultures.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous Ha: Breath of Life evening show — a breathtaking theatrical performance featuring fire dancing, traditional music, and the story of a young Polynesian man's journey. Dinner buffet is included with most ticket packages.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local café or hotel before the drive to the North Shore.
meals.lunch: Ali'i Luau buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with premium ticket packages. Features traditional Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes including kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia.
meals.dinner: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with the evening show package. A generous spread of Hawaiian and American dishes. Book the Ambassador package for the best value combining all meals and the show.

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets online in advance — the Ambassador package offers the best value including all-day access, the Ali'i Luau, and the Ha evening show. The center is about 35 miles from Honolulu — allow 1 hour for the drive. The full experience runs from noon to approximately 9:30 PM, so plan for a full day.

day_by_day.morning: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — this iconic beach is located on Maui, so either fly to Maui or if already on Maui, head to Kaanapali Beach early. Arrive by 8:30 AM to claim a prime spot on the nearly three-mile stretch of golden sand. Rent beach chairs and umbrellas from a beachside vendor. Swim in the calm, warm waters and enjoy the stunning views of Lanai and Molokai islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Kaanapali Beach Walk — a paved oceanfront path connecting the major resorts. Stop at Whalers Village open-air mall for shopping and a break from the sun. In the late afternoon, head to Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at the north end of the beach for excellent snorkeling among sea turtles and colorful fish.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Cliff Diving Ceremony at Black Rock — every evening at sunset, a torch lighter performs a traditional Hawaiian ceremony and dives from the lava rock into the ocean. A magical, free experience for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Gazebo Restaurant in Napili (near Kaanapali) — famous for macadamia nut pancakes and ocean views. Arrive early as lines form quickly. A beloved local breakfast institution.
meals.lunch: Leilani's on the Beach at Whalers Village — casual beachfront dining with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and Hawaiian plates. Mid-range pricing with gorgeous ocean views.
meals.dinner: Hula Grill Kaanapali at Whalers Village — open-air beachfront restaurant with live Hawaiian music, fresh seafood, and a warm, family-friendly atmosphere. Mid-range to slightly upscale.

day_by_day.notes: Kaanapali Beach is consistently ranked among America's best beaches. Parking is available at Whalers Village (validated with purchase) or at the public beach access points. Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously — the Hawaiian sun is intense even on cloudy days. The cliff diving ceremony typically begins around 6:00 PM — check with local staff for the exact time.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — start the morning with a guided or self-guided tour of iconic local spots serving authentic Hawaiian plate lunches. Begin at a local favorite like Rainbow Drive-In in Honolulu for the classic plate lunch experience featuring two scoops of rice, macaroni salad, and your choice of protein (kalua pig, teriyaki beef, or mahi-mahi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the food tour with stops at Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award-winning institution) for pipikaula short ribs and laulau, and finish with shave ice at Matsumoto Shave Ice on the North Shore — a Hawaii tradition since 1951. Use the afternoon to do any last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets or the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Hawaii — enjoy a sunset beach walk and a special farewell dinner. Reflect on the trip's highlights and soak in the last moments of island life before preparing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Leonard's Bakery in Honolulu — famous for malasadas (Portuguese-style donuts rolled in sugar). A Hawaii institution and perfect final morning treat.
meals.lunch: The plate lunch food tour IS the lunch — graze across multiple stops including Rainbow Drive-In and Helena's Hawaiian Food for an authentic, affordable, and delicious Hawaiian culinary experience.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki at the Outrigger Waikiki Beach Resort — a legendary Hawaii restaurant named after Duke Kahanamoku, the father of modern surfing. Enjoy fresh fish, Hawaiian classics, and live music right on Waikiki Beach. A perfect farewell dinner. Mid-range to slightly upscale.

day_by_day.notes: Helena's Hawaiian Food is closed on weekends and Mondays — confirm hours before visiting. The Aloha Stadium Swap Meet operates Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday. Pack any purchased food items carefully if bringing local treats home — some items like fresh fruits and certain plants cannot be transported to the mainland. Begin packing in the evening and confirm return flight details. Allow extra time for airport check-in as Hawaiian airports can be busy during peak summer season.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii — Flight Alaska lands at 11:20 AM. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to the SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park area. Visit the nearby Knott's Berry Farm outdoor shopping promenade for light browsing and to get oriented. Pick up any essentials and enjoy the warm California afternoon before your Hawaii adventure truly begins.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner close to the hotel to recover from travel. Explore the local dining scene in Buena Park for a low-key but satisfying first evening.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the Alaska Airlines flight before landing
meals.lunch: Mrs. Knott's Chicken Dinner Restaurant — a Buena Park institution offering hearty comfort food perfect for post-flight hunger
meals.dinner: The Ranch Restaurant & Saloon in Anaheim — upscale American cuisine with a warm, rustic ambiance ideal for a relaxed first evening

day_by_day.notes: No major activities scheduled before arrival. Keep Day 1 light to allow the family to rest and recover from travel. Confirm all Hawaii inter-island flight or ferry bookings for the days ahead. Ensure all snorkeling gear, sunscreen, and beach essentials are packed.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early from the hotel for Honolulu International Airport (LAX or SNA) for your flight to Oahu, Hawaii. Upon arrival in Honolulu, transfer via private luxury shuttle to your premium beachfront resort in Waikiki. Check in and enjoy a welcome amenity from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for your first taste of Hawaii. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas through the resort concierge. Let the kids splash in the gentle surf while adults soak in the iconic Diamond Head backdrop. Arrange a private surf lesson for the family through the resort's beach activity desk.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Waikiki sunset from the beach, then head to a rooftop or oceanfront restaurant for a celebratory first-night-in-Hawaii dinner.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the hotel before airport departure or grab-and-go from a premium airport lounge
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — an iconic beachfront restaurant serving fresh Hawaiian fish tacos, burgers, and tropical cocktails with stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — world-class Japanese-Peruvian fusion cuisine in a sophisticated setting, perfect for a luxury family celebration dinner

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights well in advance. Recommend staying at the Moana Surfrider, A Westin Resort & Spa or The Royal Hawaiian for an authentic luxury Waikiki experience. Confirm private surf lesson booking with the resort concierge upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Depart early (7:00 AM recommended) via private car to beat the crowds at this world-renowned marine sanctuary. The bay's calm, crystal-clear waters are perfect for families. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then explore the vibrant coral reef teeming with tropical fish including Humuhumunukunukuapua'a (Hawaii's state fish). Rent premium snorkeling gear on-site or bring your own.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the resort pool or beach. Arrange a private catamaran sunset sail booking for later in the week through the concierge. Kids can enjoy resort water activities while adults unwind with spa treatments.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Waikiki dining and entertainment scene. Walk along Kalakaua Avenue and enjoy the vibrant street performers and luxury boutique shopping.

meals.breakfast: Early in-room dining or resort breakfast buffet before departing for Hanauma Bay — fuel up well before snorkeling
meals.lunch: Hanauma Bay has a snack bar on-site; alternatively pack a premium picnic prepared by the resort or stop at Kaimana Beach Hotel's Hau Tree restaurant on the return
meals.dinner: Orchids at Halekulani — one of Honolulu's most celebrated fine dining restaurants with breathtaking oceanfront views and exceptional Pacific Rim cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — book at least 2 days ahead as entry is strictly limited to protect the ecosystem. Entry fee applies. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Best snorkeling is in the morning when water visibility is highest. August weather may bring occasional afternoon showers — carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — Depart by 9:00 AM via private car or luxury shuttle to the Polynesian Cultural Center on Oahu's North Shore (approximately 1 hour drive). Spend the morning exploring the six authentic Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire making, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center. Enjoy the canoe pageant on the lagoon — a spectacular floating cultural parade. Kids will love the interactive demonstrations and the chance to try traditional games and crafts from across Polynesia.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a breathtaking theatrical production featuring over 100 performers, fire dancers, and traditional music celebrating the Polynesian journey of life. This is a must-see highlight of any Hawaii family trip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — try the resort's signature Hawaiian breakfast with fresh tropical fruits, macadamia nut pancakes, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — an extensive spread of authentic Polynesian and Hawaiian dishes including kalua pork, poi, and fresh island fruits
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — an immersive premium luau experience with traditional imu-cooked kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia dessert served under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Book the 'Ambassador Package' at the Polynesian Cultural Center for the best premium experience including priority seating, guided tours, and exclusive access. The full day runs approximately 12 hours — wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen. The evening show typically ends around 9:30 PM. Arrange private car pickup in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — Embark on a guided premium food tour of Oahu's most iconic plate lunch spots. Start in Honolulu's Chinatown and work your way through legendary local institutions. Sample classic Hawaiian comfort food including kalua pork, loco moco, macaroni salad, rice, and fresh poke. Learn about the cultural history of the plate lunch tradition from your knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic Iolani Palace — the only royal palace on American soil — for a premium guided tour. Explore the beautifully restored rooms of Hawaii's last monarchs, King Kalakaua and Queen Liliuokalani. Afterward, browse the luxury boutiques at Ala Moana Center, the world's largest open-air shopping mall, for premium Hawaiian souvenirs and designer goods.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private sunset catamaran sail along the Waikiki coastline with Diamond Head as your backdrop. Many luxury operators offer champagne, fresh fruit, and light appetizers on board. Watch for spinner dolphins and sea turtles along the way.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast at the resort — save your appetite for the food tour
meals.lunch: The food tour itself serves as lunch — highlights include stops at Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award winner), Rainbow Drive-In, and a premium poke bowl at Ono Seafood
meals.dinner: MW Restaurant by Michelle Karr-Ueoka and Wade Ueoka — a celebrated Honolulu fine dining destination showcasing modern Hawaii Regional Cuisine with locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Book the food tour with a reputable local operator such as Oahu Food Tours for a premium guided experience. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the food tour and palace visit. The catamaran sunset sail should be booked in advance — recommend Maitai Catamaran or a private charter for a luxury family experience. August evenings are warm and beautiful for sailing.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Maui (OGG) on an early inter-island flight (approximately 30 minutes). Transfer via private luxury car to your premium resort in Kaanapali. Check in and enjoy a welcome amenity. The Kaanapali resort strip is home to some of Hawaii's finest luxury properties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — Head straight to the legendary Kaanapali Beach, consistently ranked among America's best beaches. Enjoy nearly three miles of golden sand and calm, turquoise waters. Rent premium beach equipment through the resort including paddleboards, kayaks, and snorkeling gear. Snorkel around Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) — a famous lava promontory teeming with sea turtles and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Witness the spectacular Black Rock cliff diving ceremony at sunset — a nightly tradition at the Sheraton Maui where a torch-lit diver leaps from the lava rock into the ocean. Stroll along the Kaanapali Beachwalk for shopping and dining.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Honolulu resort or airport lounge before the inter-island flight
meals.lunch: Leilani's on the Beach at Whalers Village — an iconic Kaanapali beachfront restaurant with fresh seafood, burgers, and stunning ocean views
meals.dinner: Japengo at Hyatt Regency Maui — award-winning Pacific Rim cuisine with fresh sushi, sashimi, and creative cocktails in an elegant oceanfront setting

day_by_day.notes: Recommend staying at the Hyatt Regency Maui Resort & Spa or Westin Maui Resort & Spa for a premium Kaanapali experience. Book inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines for the most reliable service. The Black Rock cliff diving ceremony begins at sunset — arrive 15 minutes early for the best viewing spot. Kaanapali Beach can have stronger surf in August — supervise young children near the water.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana — Embark on one of the world's most scenic drives along Maui's northeastern coastline. Hire a private luxury driver-guide for the full experience. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, explore the lush Waikamoi Nature Trail, and marvel at the dramatic Wailua Falls. The winding road passes through 59 bridges and 617 curves through breathtaking rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana journey, stopping at the black sand beach at Waianapanapa State Park — a dramatic volcanic landscape with sea caves and blowholes. Explore the sacred Hana Cultural Center and the serene Hamoa Beach, often called the most beautiful beach in the Pacific. Take a dip in the crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaanapali via private car (or arrange to stay overnight in Hana for an ultra-premium experience at Travaasa Hana). Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort spa with a traditional lomilomi massage.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — the Road to Hana is a full-day commitment
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort or stop at Nahiku Marketplace for fresh coconut, banana bread, and local snacks along the road — a beloved Road to Hana tradition
meals.dinner: Merriman's Maui in Kapalua — farm-to-table fine dining by celebrated chef Peter Merriman, featuring locally sourced Hawaiian ingredients with panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 65 miles one way and takes 3-4 hours without stops — plan for a full 10-12 hour day. A private driver-guide is strongly recommended for families so everyone can enjoy the scenery without driving stress. Waianapanapa State Park requires advance reservations. Bring motion sickness medication for children sensitive to winding roads. August may bring rain on the Hana side — pack light rain jackets.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Haleakala Crater — Wake up at 3:00 AM for the drive to Haleakala National Park summit (10,023 feet elevation). Arrive before dawn to witness one of the world's most spectacular sunrises above the clouds. The volcanic crater landscape is otherworldly and unforgettable. Bring warm layers — summit temperatures can drop to near freezing even in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakala and enjoy a premium downhill bicycle tour through the volcano's slopes with a reputable luxury operator. Alternatively, return to Kaanapali for a relaxing afternoon at the resort pool and beach. Treat the family to a premium resort spa experience — many Kaanapali resorts offer family spa packages.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Hawaiian luau on Maui. The Old Lahaina Luau is widely considered the most authentic and intimate luau experience in Hawaii, featuring traditional hula, imu ceremony, and a premium open bar with fresh Hawaiian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Pack premium snacks and hot beverages in a thermos for the Haleakala summit — resort can prepare an early morning to-go bag
meals.lunch: Mama's Fish House in Paia — one of Hawaii's most celebrated and iconic restaurants, featuring the freshest fish caught daily by local fishermen, with each dish noting the fisherman's name and catch location
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau — a complete premium dining and cultural entertainment experience included in the luau package

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise reservations are MANDATORY and must be booked weeks in advance through recreation.gov — this is non-negotiable. Dress in warm layers (temperatures near 40°F/4°C at summit). The Old Lahaina Luau is extremely popular — book 2-3 months in advance. Mama's Fish House also requires advance reservations. This is a very early morning — consider an afternoon nap before the luau.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Maui (OGG) to Kona (KOA) on the Big Island for a day trip to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park. Transfer via private luxury SUV from Kona Airport to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (approximately 1.5 hours). Enter the park and begin exploring at the Kilauea Visitor Center to understand the volcanic landscape and current activity levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — Drive the 11-mile Crater Rim Drive around the Kilauea caldera, stopping at dramatic overlooks including the Jaggar Museum overlook and steam vents. Walk through the eerie Thurston Lava Tube — a 500-year-old lava tunnel. Drive the Chain of Craters Road down to the coast to see ancient lava flows meeting the Pacific Ocean. Witness the raw, primal power of one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: If volcanic activity permits, visit the Kilauea Overlook after dark for a potentially spectacular view of the glowing lava lake — one of the most awe-inspiring natural spectacles on Earth. Return to Kona for a late dinner before flying back to Maui or Oahu.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast in Maui before the inter-island flight
meals.lunch: Cafe Ono at the Volcano House Hotel — a historic lodge perched on the rim of Kilauea caldera offering stunning crater views with your meal
meals.dinner: Brown's Beach House at the Fairmont Orchid, Kohala Coast — an exceptional oceanfront fine dining experience featuring Hawaii Regional Cuisine with fresh local seafood and premium steaks

day_by_day.notes: Check current volcanic activity status at nps.gov/havo before the visit — activity levels change frequently. The park is open 24 hours and the night lava glow (if active) is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Wear closed-toe shoes and long pants for lava field walking. Volcanic fumes (vog) can be irritating — bring masks for sensitive family members. This is a long day — depart Maui by 7:00 AM and expect to return by 10:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — Return to Oahu (or depart from Maui/Kona depending on routing). Enjoy a leisurely final morning at the resort. Take one last swim in the ocean, collect shells, and soak in the aloha spirit. Visit the resort gift shop for premium Hawaiian souvenirs including Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, and locally made jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before departure, visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial for a moving and historically significant experience. The USS Arizona Memorial and Battleship Missouri offer profound insight into Hawaii's pivotal role in World War II history. Alternatively, enjoy a final luxury spa treatment or beachside massage.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Honolulu International Airport via private luxury car for your return flight to the mainland. Depart Hawaii with unforgettable memories of beaches, volcanoes, culture, and aloha.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final resort breakfast — order the full Hawaiian spread one last time including fresh papaya, Kona coffee, and macadamia nut French toast
meals.lunch: Alan Wong's Honolulu — if routing through Oahu, this is the crown jewel of Hawaii Regional Cuisine by the legendary chef who helped define modern Hawaiian cooking
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal — request a premium meal option on your return flight, or grab a final poke bowl from Ono Seafood near the airport

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor requires advance reservations for the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour — book online at recreation.gov. Allow at least 3 hours at the airport for international/mainland check-in. Consider shipping any large souvenir purchases home via the resort's concierge service to avoid baggage fees. Mahalo for an incredible 10-day Hawaii adventure — the aloha spirit will stay with your family long after you return home.
